flashcard_questions.q: What is free will in religious teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: The God-given ability to choose freely between good and evil.

flashcard_questions.q: What does khalifah mean in Islam?
flashcard_questions.a: A steward — someone entrusted by Allah with looking after his creation.

flashcard_questions.q: What is zakah in Islamic practice?
flashcard_questions.a: Charitable giving, one of the Five Pillars, sharing wealth with those in need.
An offence motivated by hostility towards a person’s identity.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Qur’an verse says even an atom’s weight of good will be seen?
Which Bible verse says God saw everything he had made and it was very good?
Why might religious believers show compassion to someone who steals from poverty?
flashcard_questions.a: They may have stolen only to feed their family and survive.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do religious believers argue addicts need treatment rather than punishment?
flashcard_questions.a: They may not be fully in control of their actions.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Bible verse warns that the love of money is a root of evil?
What is civil disobedience as a reason for crime?
flashcard_questions.a: Deliberately breaking a law you believe to be morally wrong.

flashcard_questions.q: Who broke segregation laws in the USA because she believed they were unjust?
What did Martin Luther King Jr argue about unjust laws?
flashcard_questions.a: An unjust law is no law at all.

flashcard_questions.q: What does “hate the sin, love the sinner” mean for Christians?
flashcard_questions.a: Condemn the crime, but show compassion to the criminal.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Jesus say to explain spending time with sinners?
flashcard_questions.a: It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Qur’an verse says “Do not take life, which God has made sacred”?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (free will, khalifah, zakah, hate crime), 4 belief→source (Qur’an 99:7–8, Genesis 1:31, 1 Timothy 6:10, Qur’an 6:151), 3 cause→effect (poverty, addiction, hate the sin), 2 person cards (Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King Jr), 2 concept cards (civil disobedience, Jesus on sinners). Dropped 'good', 'evil', 'theft' and 'murder' as bare glossary terms that interfere.
